text.p: Kyotaru Co Ltd, which sought protection from creditors under Japan's bankruptcy laws in January, said on Friday that the amount by which its liabilities exceed its assets was larger than the figure it gave in January.

A spokesman for the sushi restaurant chain said the company's liabilities exceeded its assets by 70.11 billion yen, compared with the earlier figure of 39.08 billion yen which it based on financial data up to October 31, 1996.
News of the upward revision in the figure pushed down share prices in Katokichi Co Ltd, an administrator of Kyotaru's assets, on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on Friday morning, traders said.
Katokichi's shares were down 60 yen at 2,080 at midday.
Shares of Kyotaru have been delisted from the exchange.

In March, the Tokyo District Court named the president of frozen food producer Katokichi as an administrator of Kyotaru's assets, assigning Katokichi the role of supervising Kyotaru's rehabilitation and possibly offering necessary assistance.
